title: Satellite Imagery
answer: Satellite imagery as alternative data refers to the use of overhead optical, radar, and multispectral images to measure economic activity that is not captured in standard financial statements or government releases. Practitioners track things like shipping traffic, construction progress, crop health, retail parking lot occupancy, and nighttime lights. crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Satellite imagery as alternative data refers to the use of overhead optical, radar, and multispectral images to measure economic activity that is not captured in standard financial statements or government releases. Practitioners track things like shipping traffic, construction progress, crop health, retail parking lot occupancy, and nighttime lights. The field sits within alternative data because the images are collected continuously and can be processed into time series that inform macroeconomic and company level analysis.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on cloud compute and storage because raw satellite scenes are large and arrive frequently. Processing pipelines typically combine geospatial databases, object storage, and GPU instances for model inference. Many teams use Python libraries for raster and vector data handling, and they rely on commercial imagery APIs or direct downlinks from satellite operators.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The core method is to convert pixels into structured indicators. Analysts georeference and orthorectify scenes, then apply convolutional neural networks or segmentation models to detect objects such as ships, buildings, vehicles, or fields. Detections are aggregated over a region and time window to produce counts, areas, or change metrics, which are then compared against economic variables like sales, output, or trade flows.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on imagery licensing, resolution limits, and privacy. Commercial providers impose terms on redistribution and derived products, while some jurisdictions restrict high resolution imaging of sensitive sites. Analysts must also manage provenance so that a model's training data, scene dates, and cloud masks are documented, because a mislabeled or outdated image can quietly corrupt a downstream indicator. There is no single regulator for satellite derived alternative data, but securities and data protection rules still apply to how the signals are used and shared.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward higher revisit rates, cheaper small satellite constellations, and more automated feature extraction. As foundation models for remote sensing mature, teams are likely to shift from building bespoke detectors to fine tuning general purpose geospatial models. The main open question is whether the edge from satellite data persists as the imagery becomes more widely available and the processing more standardized.
